public_rationale: Stanford's report places the top four models within 25 Arena points in March 2026, showing convergence on that benchmark [e1]. A survey report published by Andreessen Horowitz on January 30, 2026 describes rising switching costs that reinforce early enterprise footholds, suggesting a possible advantage beyond benchmark performance [e2]. Neither source establishes equivalent technology and training data, or whether any provider had a durable competitive advantage on June 2, 2026 [e1, e2]. They do not establish that shared technology and data caused an absence of moats [e1, e2].
limitations: The observations precede June 2, 2026; the Stanford report became available on June 29.
Similar Arena scores do not establish interchangeable technology, equivalent training data or similarity across all capabilities.
Reported switching costs do not establish a durable competitive advantage at the claim date.
Neither source isolates the claimed causal relationship.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Because everybody competing to build AI is building essentially the same technical solution with essentially the same data, there is no moat for any of them.
conditions: everybody is building essentially the same technical solution with essentially the same data

statement.excerpt: But everybody is building essentially the same technical solution with essentially the same data, so there is no moat.
statement.document_title: Why things will eventually fall apart

our_interpretation: The context concerns competing general-purpose generative AI model providers, rather than every business using AI.
A moat means a durable competitive advantage that rivals cannot readily copy or overcome.
Essentially the same allows implementation differences. A shared architecture alone does not establish equivalent capabilities or training data.
The claim concerns the situation at publication. Earlier measurements provide context; later developments do not automatically establish what held then.
Benchmark convergence is relevant but cannot by itself establish the absence of advantages in distribution, switching costs, proprietary data or infrastructure.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes substantially interchangeable technology and data among the relevant providers, and shows that this similarity prevents any provider from maintaining a durable competitive advantage.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes a durable competitive advantage for at least one relevant provider, or material technological or data differences that defeat the asserted causal explanation. A temporary benchmark lead alone is insufficient.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable technical and training-data disclosures, together with longitudinal evidence establishing conditions on June 2, 2026, could settle the claim. Support requires showing that substantial similarity prevented durable competitive advantages. A demonstrated durable advantage for a relevant provider, or material technology or data differences that defeat the causal explanation, would contradict it.
